description: Simulator presets and battery defaults. Sizes of solar, battery and generator fleet are example inputs, not data; every other value cites its source.

sources.text: NLR (formerly NREL) Annual Technology Baseline 2025, Utility-Scale Battery Storage, section Roundtrip Efficiency (based on Cole et al. 2025). Other sources range from 83% (PNNL Energy Storage Cost and Performance Database v2024, LFP and NMC) to 92% (Lazard LCOE+ 2026, low-cost 4-hour case).
PNNL (2022) Grid Energy Storage Technology Cost and Performance Assessment, PNNL-33283: baseline depth of discharge 80% for LFP and NMC (section 1, p. 4). Lazard LCOE+ 2026 models 90%.

lagos.label: Lagos: diesel generators
lagos.example_note: Example scenario: 1,000 small commercial generators. No count of generators in Lagos is published, so the number of generators and the solar and battery sizes are example inputs you can change.

sources.text: Average commercial generator size 7.5 kVA, from a consumer survey in Aba: World Bank (2014) Diesel Power Generation: Inventories and Black Carbon Emissions in Nigeria, p. 17.

Load factor 50% where generators run full time (40% for back-up use): World Bank (2014), footnote 6, p. 17. 7.5 kVA × 50% = 3.75 kW, taking kVA as kW. IFC (2019) notes the kVA rating is typically 1 to 1.5 times the kW load, so real output may be up to a third lower.
Running 06:00 to 24:00, 18 hours a day: some Nigerian generators run 15 to 18 hours a day, World Bank (2014), p. 1.
About half of Lagos energy demand is met by diesel and petrol generators: World Bank (2020) The Cost of Air Pollution in Lagos, chapter 3, p. 11.
Solar profile: PVGIS 5.3 hourly output for Ikeja, Lagos (6.60 N, 3.35 E), year 2023, in West Africa Time (UTC+1).

Generator emission factors: US EPA AP-42 section 3.3, with the range from World Bank (2014) Table 13. Damage costs: no Nigerian values exist, so euros are a rough transfer from the EEA European average.

grid.label: Grid average: pick a country
grid.example_note: Example scenario: a site drawing a steady 10 MW from the grid. Pick a country; its grid mix is Ember's latest year.

sources.text: Grid mix: Ember yearly electricity data, the country's latest year (CC BY 4.0).
Solar: PVGIS 5.3, a typical day for each month at one point inside the country (a rough national profile).
